theme.title: The beautiful game
theme.subtitle: San Antonio, 2013–14
theme.recap: The Spurs passed Miami off the floor in the 2014 Finals, a year after losing to them, with a record ten international players.

questions.prompt: The 2013–14 Spurs' longest winning streak lasted how many games?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Emboldened by a 19-game winning streak from late February to early April, including an unbeaten month in March (16–0)

funFacts.text: San Antonio's title was revenge for a heartbreaking Finals loss to Miami the previous season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Spurs avenged their 2013 NBA Finals loss and became NBA champions

funFacts.text: The team's run included an undefeated March, a remarkable display of consistency across a packed schedule.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including an unbeaten month in March (16–0)

funFacts.text: Dallas nearly ruined the championship march, taking the Spurs to the limit in the opening playoff round.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Mavericks in the regular season for 2 consecutive years. San Antonio won 4–3

questions.prompt: The 2013–14 Spurs opened the season with an NBA-record number of international players. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They also entered the season with an NBA-record ten international players.

funFacts.text: French forward Boris Diaw became a key ball-mover on the championship roster.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Diaw led all players in the series in assists

funFacts.text: The team's system spread minutes so widely that no Spur averaged half an hour during the regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: no player averaging 30 minutes during the regular season

funFacts.text: The Finals marked the return of a less punishing travel format, partly enabled by charter flights.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: as well as the increased use of chartered flights as opposed to commercial flights

questions.prompt: In the first half of Game 3 of the 2014 Finals, what percentage of their shots did the Spurs make?
questions.note: 75.8%, a Finals record for a half.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a Finals-record 75.8% shooting effort from the team during the first half

funFacts.text: Popovich inserted Boris Diaw into the starting five, opening up extra passing lanes against Miami.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: San Antonio's insertion of Boris Diaw into the starting lineup created more ball movement

funFacts.text: Kawhi Leonard began the game with a perfect string of made shots and set a new personal scoring high.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Leonard, limited to only 18 points in the first two games, made his first six shots

funFacts.text: Miami hadn't lost at home in that postseason before San Antonio's sudden offensive explosion.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat, who had been 8–0 at home in the playoffs

questions.prompt: How many of the 2014 Spurs' playoff wins came by 15 points or more?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Spurs finished the playoffs with 12 wins by 15 points or more, the most ever in the postseason.

funFacts.text: Kawhi Leonard won Finals MVP, becoming the youngest recipient since Magic Johnson.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: and the youngest since Magic Johnson in 1982

funFacts.text: Tim Duncan surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's all-time postseason minutes mark during the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Duncan also eclipsed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's previous mark

funFacts.text: Miami's other starters struggled as LeBron James tried to carry the offense on his own.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: their other starters combined for only 28 points on 32 percent shooting

questions.prompt: By how many points per game did the Spurs outscore Miami in the 2014 Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Spurs outscored the Heat in the series by the largest per game average point differential (14.0) in Finals history.

funFacts.text: Game One's air-conditioning failure turned the arena into a sweltering environment and left LeBron cramping.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the AT&T Center's malfunctioning air-conditioning system

funFacts.text: Miami's Game Two victory briefly leveled the rematch before San Antonio seized control on the road.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bosh made the go-ahead three-point field goal on a pass from James

funFacts.text: The Spurs clinched after overcoming a furious early Heat start in the deciding game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: San Antonio bounced back to outscore Miami 37–13 from the beginning of the second quarter
